<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIX.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|271 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>they cried, saying, Crucifie, crucifie him. Pilate saith to them, Take him you, and crucifie him. for I finde no cause in him. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=7}}† The Ievves ansvvered him, VVe haue a Law: and according to the Law he ought to die, because he hath made him self the sonne of God.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=8}}† When Pilate therfore had heard this saying, he feared more. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=9}}† And he entred into the Palace againe: and he saith to {{sc|Iesvs}}, VVhence art thou? But {{sc|Iesvs}} gaue him no ansvver. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=10}}† Pilate therfore saith to him, Speakest thou not to me? knovvest thou not that I haue povver to crucifie thee, and I haue povver to release thee? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=11}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, Thou shouldest not haue any povver against me, vnles it vvere giuen thee from aboue. Therfore he that hath betraied me to thee, hath the greater sinne.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=12}}† From thence forth Pilate sought to release him. But the Iewes cried, saying, If thou release this man, thou art not Cæsars frend. euery one that maketh him self a king, speaketh against Cæsar. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=13}}† But Pilate vvhen he had heard these vvordes, brought forth {{sc|Iesvs}}: and he sate in the iudgement seate, in the place that is called Lithóstrotos, and in Hebrevv Gábbatha. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=14}}† And it vvas the Parasceue of Pasche, about the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ He meaneth midday, counting from sunne rising. for so doth the Scripture count the houres of the day. ''Mat. 20. Mar. 15. Luc, 23. Io. 4. Act. 3 & 10''.}}∷ sixt houre, and he saith to the Ievves, Loe your king. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=15}}† But they cried, Avvay, avvay vvith him, crucifie him. Pilate saith to them, Shal I crucifie your king? The cheefe priests answered, VVe haue no king, but Cæsar. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=16}}† Then therfore he deliuered him vnto them for to be crucified.

And they tooke {{sc|Iesvs}}, and led him forth. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 27, 33. Mr. 15, 20. Lu. 23, 33.''}}* And bearing {{sup|‖}} his ovvne crosse he went forth into that vvhich is called the place of Caluarie, in Hebrevv Gólgotha. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=18}}† vvhere they crucified him, and vvith him two others, on the one side and on the other, and in the middes {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=19}}† And Pilate wrote a title also: and he put it vpon the crosse. And it vvas vvritten, {{sc|Iesvs of nazareth the king of the iewes}}. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=20}}† This title therfore many of the Ievves did reade: because the place vvhere {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas crucified, vvas nigh to the citie: and it vvas vvritten in {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ These three tongues being for other causes most famous before in al the world, are now also dedicated to God in the triumphans title of the Crosse of Christ, and in them the holy Scriptures are more conueniently written, taught, & preserued.}}∷ Hebrevv, in Greeke, and in Latin. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=21}}† The cheefe priests therfore of the Ievves said to Pilate, VVrite not, The king of the Iewes: but that he said, I am king of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=22}}† Pilate ansvvered, That vvhich I haue written, I haue vvritten.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=23}}† The {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''* Mt. 27, 35. Mr. 15, 24. Luc. 23, 34.''}}* souldiars therfore vvhen they had crucified him,<noinclude>{{rh|||tooke}}</noinclude>
